title: How do you draw the circle pictures with a compass?
description: The five circle pictures from the start of the chapter are drawn again with a ruler and a compass. The compass opening is set against a ruler, the tip is fixed at each middle spot, and the distance between tips decides whether circles touch, share a middle or overlap.
teaching_notes: One idea: the tip position and the opening of the compass decide how the circles sit. Watch for children who move the tip while drawing, which gives circles that do not close.

source: Using a ruler and a compass, recreate the artwork pictures and try to make them look as good as the book's pictures.
video_script.why: The child uses the compass method of the solved example to draw touching, shared-middle and overlapping circles.
video_script.substitution: Radius two centimetres for the first circles, and tips four centimetres and three centimetres apart.
video_script.anchor: The five artwork pictures of the book
video_script.payoff_line: Every circle is drawn with the tip fixed at its centre.

final_answer.value: all five pictures drawn with a compass; touching circles have tips two radii apart, shared-middle circles have different radii, overlapping circles have tips closer than two radii
final_answer.spoken: all five pictures are drawn with the compass; touching circles have tips two radii apart, overlapping circles have tips closer than that, and circles with a shared middle have different radii

never_show: the finished pictures before the answer
maths_rules: Touching circles: radius 2 cm, tips 2 cm + 2 cm = 4 cm apart.
Shared middle: the same tip point, radii 2 cm and 1 cm; 1 cm is half of 2 cm.
Overlapping circles: radius 2 cm, tips 3 cm apart; 3 cm < 4 cm, so they overlap.
Mouse face: 1 face + 2 ears + 2 eyes = 5 circles, all drawn with the compass.
Check: the tip distance for touching circles is 2 x 2 = 4 cm.
video_script.design: One idea: the position of the tip and the opening fix each circle. Uses the compass method of the example in the book. Open ended question with one worked choice of radius.

marks.centre: the fixed point gets the label centre
marks.radius: the opening between the tip and the pencil gets the label radius

narration: <bookmark mark='tip'/>A compass draws a circle when its tip stays fixed on one point.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>That fixed point is called the centre of the circle.
<bookmark mark='radius'/>The opening of the compass is called the radius of the circle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: compass opened to 2 cm against a ruler

narration: <bookmark mark='set'/>Step one, in the same way as the example in your book, set the compass against a ruler.
Open it to two centimetres for the first circles.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: tips 4 cm apart (2 + 2); two circles of radius 2 cm touch at one place

marks.first: the first circle is drawn with the tip on its centre
marks.touch: the tip moves four centimetres away and the second circle touches the first

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, for two touching circles, draw the first circle with the tip on a point.
<bookmark mark='touch'/>Move the tip four centimetres away, which is two plus two.
Draw the second circle there.
The two circles touch at one place.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: same tip point, opening 1 cm; a small circle inside the circle of radius 2 cm

marks.same: the tip stays on the same point
marks.small: the opening is changed to one centimetre and a smaller circle appears inside

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, for circles with a shared middle, keep the tip on the same point.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Change the opening to one centimetre and draw the smaller circle inside.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: opening 2 cm; tips 3 cm apart, 3 < 4; three circles in a row, each overlapping the next

marks.row: three tip points are marked three centimetres apart
marks.overlap: three circles are drawn and each overlaps the next

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Step four, for three overlapping circles, keep the opening at two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='overlap'/>Place the tips three centimetres apart.
That is less than four, so each circle overlaps the next.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: mouse face of five circles; the dot and mouth with a ruler; crossing lines with a small circle at each bottom end

marks.mouse: a big circle and four small circles form the mouse face
marks.sizes: the big circle and the small circles light up in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='mouse'/>Step five, for the mouse face, draw all five circles with the compass.
<bookmark mark='sizes'/>Use a big one for the face, and small ones for the ears and the eyes.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Draw the mouth and the crossing lines with the ruler.
Draw the small circles at the line ends with the compass.

beats.on_screen: Step 6: check by measuring the tips: touching 4 cm = 2 x 2; overlapping 3 cm, less than 4 cm

marks.check: a ruler measures the distance between the tips of each pair of circles
marks.more: the four centimetre reading is circled for the touching circles

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check by measuring the distance between the tips.
<bookmark mark='more'/>For touching circles it is four centimetres, which is twice the radius.
For overlapping circles it is less than that.

beats.on_screen: Answer: all five pictures are drawn with the compass
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every circle is drawn with the tip fixed at its centre.
All five pictures are drawn with the compass, and they are round all the way.
